verdict.rationale: Helicone's docs have a dedicated self-host section stating you can "deploy your own instance of Helicone using your preferred method" with multiple deployment options, including Docker Compose for quick or small-scale setups. The pricing page and llms.txt describe it as open-source/OSS. The community note about the Commons Clause concerns license labeling, not whether you can self-host, so it creates no dispute. Missing for 10: detail on deployment methods beyond Docker Compose (e.g. production-scale or Kubernetes options), confirmation that self-hosted instances carry feature parity with the cloud core, and independent hands-on reports of self-hosting.
